jobs.occupation: Associate Partner with a focus on operations and supply chain transformation, Copenhagen or Aarhus
jobs.description:
Key words and Experience:

• Copenhagen or Aarhus

• Commercial growth

• Operations and Supply Chain

• Client Engagement

Are you passionate about helping clients solve complex supply chain challenges and create lasting business value? Do you combine deep functional expertise with commercial acumen, strong client relationships and leadership experience? Are you also curious about how AI, data and digital capabilities can strengthen future operations? Then you could play a key role in growing our Supply Chain & Operations practice and leading high-impact transformations.

About Valcon

We are a European powerhouse in AI and data-driven business transformation, bringing this to life by integrating management consulting with data and digital technology capabilities.

We ensure companies are in their best possible shape and fit for the future. We spot opportunities and help bring them to life. We are thorough, fast and collaborative in everything we do. From the boardroom to the shop floor. From strategy to operations.

We are a no-nonsense consultancy with curious individuals who are driven by creating value together with clients. We have an informal culture and a flat hierarchy with offices in Denmark, Sweden, the Netherlands, the UK, Germany, Croatia and Serbia.

To thrive in this role, you have demonstrated experience in these three competence areas:

• Commercial growth: Build strong client relationships, identify opportunities and contribute to the growth of existing and new client engagements through trusted advisory and business development activities

• Client engagement: Lead complex supply chain and operational improvement transformations from problem definition and solution design through implementation and value realization.

• Capability development: Help strengthen Supply Chain & Operations offerings, methodologies and market presence while leveraging AI, data and technology as key enablers of transformation

In addition, you should embody these skills:

• Supply Chain & Operations expertise: Deep experience within one or more areas such as Supply Chain Planning, S&OP, Logistics/Distribution, Procurement, Operational Excellence and Supply Chain Transformation

• People leadership: Build strong relationships, inspire teams and create an environment where people feel empowered, supported and motivated to perform

• Commercial and consulting acumen: Combine strategic thinking with a pragmatic delivery mindset and a strong understanding of how to create value for clients and grow trusted partnerships

• Digital mindset: Experience working with data, digital solutions and technology, or a strong curiosity about how these can enable better supply chain performance and business transformation

• Education: Relevant Master’s degree, fluent in English both written and spoken, Danish is a plus

Career opportunities

Valcon is in a significant growth phase supported by acquisitions and capital investment from Rivean Capital and Waterland Private Equity. This supports our ambitious expansion plans – both geographically and in terms of capabilities – with a particular focus on the Nordics and the DACH (German-speaking) region. Therefore, you will have a unique opportunity to help shape the company’s development and gain strategic influence over its future direction.

The role provides internal career development opportunities toward broader leadership roles within the capability or across the broader organisation. With Valcon’s international footprint and focus on complex Supply Chain and Operation projects in the business and technology space, you will gain access to:

• A broad network of colleagues and clients across Europe

• Strategically significant and high-complexity projects

• Opportunities to work with cutting-edge technology, including AI, data and digital technologies

Application

If this role sounds like a good match, we warmly encourage you to apply and share how your experience, strengths and perspective could contribute to the team. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

**Your impact begins here

**As Integration Project Manager, you will coordinate that data from acquisitions reaches the people who need it, when they need it. You will quickly understand the deliverables, form a plan and align stakeholders behind shared priorities and goals. Your work keeps projects moving and builds a stronger approach for future integrations.

**What You’ll Bring

**You combine structured delivery with strong stakeholder management and a practical understanding of data integration. You bring:

• Substantial experience leading complex projects across functions and organisational boundaries.

• A track record of aligning senior stakeholders, clarifying accountability and driving delivery without direct authority.

• Experience translating business needs into coordinated plans and managing dependencies, risks and competing priorities.

• An understanding of data migration or integration, including how business processes, data and IT systems relate to each other.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to make complex topics clear and actionable.

• The ability to take ownership, build trust, create momentum and work through ambiguity, challenging assumptions constructively.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**Experience with M&A integration, pharmaceutical R&D, CMC or Quality.

**What You’ll Do

**

• You will take ownership of the planning, coordination and governance of data integration, and help teams move forward when information is incomplete or circumstances change.

• Establish and drive cross-functional data integration plans with clear scope, milestones, ownership and governance.

• Align business and technical stakeholders on data requirements, priorities and delivery expectations.

• Coordinate dependencies across R&D, CMC, Quality, IT and Business Development.

• Identify and manage risks, issues and resource constraints, and escalate decisions when needed.

• Give senior stakeholders clear updates on progress, risks and decisions.

• Develop and improve ways of working for data integration, applying lessons learned across projects.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Integration Data Management in Operations and IT Quality, and work closely with colleagues across the business. In Enterprise IT & Quality, colleagues work across the Novo value chain, staying close to stakeholders and helping deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working.

Your closest partners will be colleagues in R&D, CMC, GMS Quality, Enterprise IT and Business Development.. You will manage competing priorities across multiple projects, so success depends on autonomy, sound judgement and the ability to influence without direct authority. Clear priorities, honest conversations and quick decisions will help you move each integration forward.

**What You Can Expect Here

**Our acquisition portfolio creates a varied environment. You will shape how Novo plans and delivers data integration and strengthen our approach for future acquisitions. You will build new skills through collaboration across the value chain, and you will be trusted to take ownership, make your voice heard and perform at your best.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000 to 956,900 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to bring clarity to complex acquisition data integrations, apply for the Integration Project Manager role by 16 November 2026.

For further information, please contact Linda Pedersen at lsjq@novonordisk.com

Are you interested in using AI to create relevant, high-quality content for audiences across global markets? We are looking for an AI Content Designer to help regional teams localize visual content efficiently while ensuring it remains aligned with the Jabra brand.

In the role of our AI-Powered Content Designer in the Global Brand, Content & Digital team you will use Leonardo, our internal AI-powered content tool, to create and localize visual assets that make campaigns relevant across regions.

**The Team You Will Be Part Of

**You will join the Design team within Global Brand, Content & Digital, a creative function responsible for content across Jabra launches and campaigns. Reporting to the Senior Design Lead, you will collaborate with colleagues across Design, Content, Brand and regional marketing teams.

This is a new role in the team and an opportunity to help shape how we use AI to scale regional content. We value curiosity, collaboration and a structured approach to creating content that is visually engaging, relevant and on-brand.

**Your Contribution Is Appreciated, And You Will

**

• Use Leonardo, GN’s internal AI-powered content tool, to create and localize visual assets for regional campaigns and marketing activities

• Translate regional briefs, market needs and feedback into relevant image variations across content types and channels

• Work closely with regional stakeholders and colleagues, including Luca, to clarify requirements and deliver content that meets local needs

• Review content for visual quality, brand alignment, cultural relevance and technical specifications before delivery

• Adapt existing campaign assets and generate new regional imagery that supports local activation

• Maintain organized files, templates and workflows to enable efficient production and reuse of content

• Explore opportunities to improve AI-supported content workflows and share learnings with the wider Design team

**To perform well in the role, we imagine that you:

**

• Bring a background in graphic design and an understanding of how visual content is developed for different channels and formats

• Are interested in AI-powered creative tools and ready to build experience using Leonardo and related technologies

• Have a solid visual judgement and an eye for creating clear, engaging and brand-aligned imagery

• Communicate clearly, ask thoughtful questions and work well with colleagues across creative, commercial and regional teams

• Are curious, structured and self-managing, with the ability to manage several requests and incorporate feedback constructively

At GN we pride ourselves on encouraging flexible work whenever possible. We trust our people to fulfill their responsibilities, to know when in-person collaboration is better than hybrid, and to be present when it's needed most.

**We encourage you to apply

**Even if you don’t match all the above-mentioned skills, we welcome your application if you think you have transferable skills. We highly value a mindset and motivation that align with our core values, to not only ensure growth for you, but for your team and the wider GN organization as well.

**We are focused on an inclusive recruitment process

**All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. As such, we encourage you to submit your CV without a photo to ensure an equal and fair application process.

Should you have any special requirements for the interview, please let the Hiring Manager know upon accepting the invitation to the interview.

**How to apply?

**Use the ‘APPLY’ link no later than November 15th. Applications are assessed continuously, so don’t wait to send yours.

**Join us in bringing people closer

**GN brings people closer through our advanced intelligent hearing, audio, video, and gaming solutions. Inspired by people and motivated by innovation, we deliver technology that enhances the senses of hearing and sight. We enable people with hearing loss to overcome real-life problems, improve communication and collaboration for businesses, and provide great experiences for audio and gaming users.

GN Store Nord A/S has entered into a definitive agreement for the sale of GN’s Hearing business to Amplifon S.p.A. to create a global leader in audiology. For GN Group, this creates an opportunity to expand our position in the large audio and video peripherals markets. Read more about the announcement HERE.

**We hope you will join us on this journey and look forward to receiving your application.

**

Would you enjoy leading drug development for rare conditions? Are you a medic with experience designing clinical trials and interacting with regulatory authorities?

_If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Medical Director, Clinical Development, Endocrine & Rare Diseases

_

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking an energetic and passionate Medical Director to join our team. As a member of the Ascendis Pharma team, you will play a crucial role in driving the design, safety monitoring, and data analysis within the Endocrine and Rare Disease Medical Sciences area. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

You will join the Clinical Development team, being part of the Endocrine & Rare Disease Medical Sciences organization. You will report directly to the VP of Clinical Science who is based in the US. You will be based in Hellerup together with the Danish team.

Since you will join a team based in different time zones, you must be available for evening meetings. This position also may require occasional international travel.

Your key responsibilities will be

• Contribute to formulation and implementation of the Clinical Development Plan

• Leverage medical expertise and hands-on clinical experience to promote relevance and rigor of the development program

• For clinical trials: design, provide overall oversight, and support site and subject retention

• Serve as a Medical Monitor for clinical trials, ensure study integrity, and track accumulating safety and efficacy data

• Provide leadership to teams of medical monitors and study teams

• Ensure successful completion of trial-related documents (including clinical trial protocols, investigator brochures, medical monitoring plans, site training materials, clinical study reports, health authority responses, standard operating procedures, etc.) with cross-functional team members

• Ensure study integrity, and track accumulating safety and efficacy data

• Analyze, evaluate, interpret, and report clinical data

• Anticipate and solve complex drug development problems

• Contribute to regulatory strategy

• Contribute to drafting and reviewing of clinical documents, manuscripts, presentations, and regulatory submissions

• Maintain up-to-date knowledge of relevant science, medical information, good clinical practices, and regulatory guidance

• Collaborate with—and serve as a clinical research resource for—cross-functional colleagues (e.g. in clinical operations, statistics, regulatory affairs, medical affairs, health economics outcomes research, commercial, finance) to optimize product development

• Contribute to (and may be asked to represent the clinical development department in) corporate strategic and organizational initiatives

• Cultivate relationships with investigative sites, clinical consultants, and key opinion leaders to represent the interests of the company

• Assist in portfolio management and commercial activities as needed

• Complete assigned tasks thoroughly, accurately, and on time

• Adhere to rigorous ethical standards

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold an M.D. degree and preferably also a Ph.D. degree. You have hands-on experience treating patients.

Furthermore, you have:

• At least 5-7 years of industry experience (other relevant experience e.g., post-graduate experience in the clinical and/or academic realms may also be considered on a case-by-case basis).

• Strong track record of scientific and clinical inquiry

• Possess excellent communication skills (written and oral)

• Demonstrate sound judgement in terms of handling complex, confidential, and regulated information

Key competencies:

You have a proven ability to learn quickly, even in fast‑paced environments.

You take ownership of your work, lead by example, and collaborate effectively with colleagues across the organization. You are trusted by others for your sound judgment and discretion, particularly when handling confidential, sensitive, or regulated information.

To succeed in the position, we expect you to be comfortable working with complex instructions, managing multiple priorities, and consistently maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.

Travel: 20-30 days per year

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

A note to recruiters:

We do not allow external search party solicitation. Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team (specifically from: Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director) is not allowed. If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

jobs.occupation: Project Director, Commercial Market Readiness Lead, Demant Hearing Aids
jobs.description:
Drive Market Readiness for the Next Generations of Hearing Solutions

At Demant Hearing Aids, we are transforming how we bring innovation to market through our new Product-to-Success (P2S) framework. As a global organization with a strong cadence of product launches, our competitiveness depends on turning innovation into meaningful value for our customers and users.

We are looking for a commercially minded and highly collaborative Project Director, Commercial Market Readiness. This is a new role in which you will bring the voice of the markets into global product development and launch planning. You will also ensure that global plans are translated into market-ready execution, so our innovations deliver successful commercial outcomes.

As a key member of the Program Management Team (PMT), you will lead Market Readiness deliveries across Marketing, Sales, Training, and Service. Your objective is to ensure that the commercial organization is fully prepared to launch new products successfully.

This role sits at the intersection of commercial strategy, program execution, and cross-functional leadership. You will connect activities across the Growth Engine (Global Marketing) and Revenue Engine (Global Sales), creating alignment and ensuring coordinated execution. We are recruiting two new Market Readiness colleagues for this role, who will alternate lead responsibility across releases, giving each release one clear Market Readiness lead (internally referred to as NMRI). The roles will report to the respective commercial leaders in Marketing and Sales.

Experience from a market organization, sales company, or another market-facing role will be a strong advantage, giving you valuable insight into customer needs, commercial execution, product adoption, and market impact.

Your Responsibilities

As our Commercial Market Readiness Lead, you will:

Lead Market Readiness in the Program Management Team

• Communicate global strategies and launch plans ensuring locally executable plans and launch readiness across markets.

• Champion market needs and launch realities within the program, ensuring decisions reflect the perspectives of customers and users, hearing care professionals and sales companies.

• Represent Market Readiness in the PMT and ensure timely, high-quality delivery against agreed milestones.

• Coordinate cross-functional activities and provide clear visibility of progress, risks, dependencies, quality, compliance, and overall readiness.

• Enable confident and timely decisions through concise status reporting, clear recommendations, and early escalation of critical issues.

Act as a Commercial and Strategic Leader

• Ensure market readiness activities align with broader business objectives and commercial ambitions.

• Drive collaboration across global and local functions, ensuring market perspectives influence key program decisions and that solutions are practical, scalable, and relevant for local execution.

• Translate market insights and commercial realities into actionable recommendations for the program and leadership teams.

What You Bring

We are looking for an experienced leader who combines strong commercial understanding and market understanding with excellent project and stakeholder management capabilities. As this is a new role, you will have a unique opportunity to shape and establish it together with colleagues across the global and local value chain.

Experience

• First-hand experience in a market-facing role or in close partnership with sales companies, with the ability to bring an outside-in perspective to program decisions.

• Significant experience in commercial project leadership, product launches, market readiness, or a related field.

• Proven ability to navigate complex stakeholder landscapes and influence without direct authority.

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in business or a related field, combined with at least five years of experience in sales, marketing, project management, or another commercial environment.

Competencies

• Lead with a strong business and commercial mindset.

• Create clarity, alignment, and momentum across diverse stakeholder groups.

• Drive predictability and transparency through disciplined planning and execution.

• Practice structured, timely, and effective communication.

• Build trust and collaboration across functions and organizational levels.

How to apply

If you thrive in a dynamic environment where commercial impact, stakeholder leadership, and program excellence come together, we would love to hear from you.

To apply, please submit your CV and a short motivation letter via our online application portal no later than November 22nd, 2026.

For further information about the position, please contact Dorthe Krogh Jensen, Vice President, Brand Management, at djen@demant.com or Steven Schmidt, Head of Global Sales at stns@demant.com

We expect to conduct first-round interviews during weeks 48-49, with second-round interviews taking place in week 50.

Join us and help turn innovation into market success.

At Demant, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of ethnicity, age, gender, personality, disability, or educational background. Diversity is an integral part of our culture, and we particularly encourage women pursuing careers in STEM to apply, supporting United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5: Gender Equality.

About Demant

Demant is a world-leading hearing healthcare and technology group built on a heritage of care, health, and innovation since 1904. The Group offers innovative technologies, solutions, and expertise to help people hear better. In every aspect, from hearing care, hearing aids and hearing implants to diagnostic equipment and services and audio solutions, Demant is active and engaged. Headquartered in Denmark, the Group employs more than 21,000 people globally and is present with solutions in 130 countries where we create life-changing hearing health and high-end audio and video solutions. William Demant Foundation holds the majority of shares in Demant A/S, which is listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen and among the 25 most traded stocks.

Are you an experienced assistant who thrives in a dynamic international environment? Do you enjoy creating structures, enabling effective decision-making and helping leadership teams execute global priorities? And are you looking for a role where your ability to bring clarity, alignment and momentum will make a real difference? Then you might be our new HR Leadership Team Assistant in Demant Group Services.

Supporting leadership excellence across global HR

As HR Leadership Team Assistant, you will play a central role in supporting Demant's Global HR Leadership Team and the newly established HR Portfolio team. Acting as a trusted coordination partner to senior HR leaders, you will help create structure, transparency and momentum across leadership activities, strategic initiatives and transformation programmes.

In this role, you will ensure that leadership processes run smoothly and efficiently. You will coordinate activities across a broad stakeholder landscape, maintain visibility of priorities and actions, and help leaders stay focused on what matters most by providing high-quality operational and organisational support.

Meet your new team and manager

You will become part of the newly established HR Transformation Portfolio team within Demant HR and work closely with colleagues across Global HR. The team is focused on enabling strategic execution, strengthening collaboration and supporting key HR initiatives across the organisation.

The position reports to Nina Castler, Head of HR Transformation Portfolio Management, and works closely with members of the Global HR Leadership Team. The position is based at the Demant Headquarters in Smørum, Copenhagen. We offer flexibility to work from home when business needs and tasks allow.

Enabling leadership effectiveness and strategic execution

The HR Leadership Team Assistant will play a key role in supporting leadership effectiveness across Global HR, ensuring alignment across stakeholders, managing critical coordination activities and helping leadership forums operate efficiently.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Coordinate HR Leadership Team meetings, governance forums and strategic initiatives involving senior stakeholders across functions, countries and time zones

• Drive agenda planning by gathering input from stakeholders

• Capture decisions, actions and deadlines while maintaining visibility and follow-up to support execution across the team

• Support planning and stakeholder coordination related to key HR transformation and operating model initiatives

• Manage complex calendars, competing priorities and leadership activities in a fast-paced global environment

• Prepare presentations, reports, organisational information and leadership materials that support informed decision-making

• Identify opportunities to improve processes, strengthen ways of working and leverage Microsoft 365 and AI tools to increase efficiency and consistency

In addition, you will help create structure and governance which enable a growing global HR organisation to collaborate effectively and deliver on its strategic ambitions.

Your qualifications & experience

We imagine that you will bring a combination of:

• Solid experience from a Team Assistant, Executive Assistant, Project Assistant, Business Support or similar role within a complex international organization supporting leadership teams and cross-functional stakeholders

• Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to navigate competing priorities across organisational levels

• Proven experience creating structure, driving coordination and ensuring follow-through in a fast-paced environment

• Experience preparing presentations, reports, meeting documentation and materials for leadership audiences

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365 tools and an interest in AI, automation and process optimisation

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken

Being highly organised, proactive and service-minded is a strong foundation for this role, and we are looking for someone who will naturally create structure in complex environments, anticipate challenges and stay one step ahead. At the same time, you are comfortable asking questions, challenging assumptions and contributing to discussions when needed. You thrive in an environment with multiple stakeholders, know how to prioritise when demands exceed capacity and build trusted relationships through professionalism, credibility and sound judgement.

Meet your new team

This is an opportunity to join a highly capable and collaborative HR leadership environment during a period of significant transformation. You will work closely with senior leaders, gain unique insight into global HR priorities and play an important role in shaping how HR operates and delivers value across the organisation.

You will become part of a team that values partnership, transparency and continuous improvement, where your contribution will be visible and where the structure you create will have a tangible impact across a global stakeholder network. For the right person, the role offers broad exposure, meaningful responsibility and opportunities to expand your scope over time.

Ready to join Demant's HR Portfolio team?

Please submit your application no later than 18th of November. Please note we only accept applications submitted via our application system in accordance with the GDPR legislation.

We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis and aim to initiate the interview process at the end of November.

We value diversity, equity, and inclusion (DE&I) and we are committed to creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome applications from alle qualified candidates regardless of ethnic background, personality, age, gender, and education. Diversity is part of our cultural DNA. Women in STEM areas are particularly encouraged to apply, as Demant supports United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5 on gender equality.

Are you excited by operating in the intersection of technology, commercial strategy, and business transformation? Do you thrive when translating complex business needs into practical system solutions that deliver measurable value across a global organisation? Then you may be our new Product owner, pricing solutions in Hearing Aids.

Take our pricing solutions to the next level

In this newly established role, you will play a key part in shaping how pricing is managed across our global business. You will join a major ERP transformation programme and take ownership of the pricing solution that connects commercial pricing strategies with operational execution. Working closely with pricing, commercial, finance, and IT stakeholders, you will help create scalable solutions that support business growth and enable better commercial decision-making.

Your impact as our new product owner, pricing solutions

As Product owner, pricing solutions, you will ensure that pricing strategies can be implemented, maintained, and continuously improved through our systems and processes. You will translate business requirements into technical solutions, drive implementation activities, and act as the key link between commercial stakeholders and IT teams.

You will play a central role in our global D365 Finance & Operations and QFO rollout programmes, helping to establish the pricing capabilities that will support our future commercial landscape. Beyond implementation, you will contribute to continuous optimisation and ensure that pricing processes remain efficient, scalable, and user-friendly.

Get to know your team and manager

You will join a newly established Commercial Pricing team within Hearing Aids, where you will have the opportunity to influence both the solutions we build and the way we work together. The team combines commercial expertise, pricing knowledge, and process excellence, and works closely with colleagues across markets, functions, and countries.

You will report to Sebastian Strauss and be based at Demant Headquarters in Smørum, Copenhagen. We offer flexibility to work from home when tasks allow. As part of a large-scale global transformation programme involving colleagues from around the world, you can expect international collaboration and approximately 30 to 40 travel days per year.

Drive pricing transformation in a global organisation

Your key responsibilities are:

• Own and drive the pricing solution across global ERP rollout programmes from requirements gathering through go-live and hypercare

• Translate commercial pricing strategies, pricing models, rebates, promotions, discounts, and agreements into scalable system solutions

• Manage and prioritise the pricing backlog, defining user stories, acceptance criteria, and business requirements

• Act as the primary business counterpart to IT, ensuring that technical solutions meet commercial objectives and operational needs

• Identify functionality gaps and design practical solutions through integrations, workflows, tools, or supporting systems

• Lead business testing activities, support releases, and contribute to training, documentation, and change management

• Drive continuous improvement of pricing processes, data structures, and governance to support long-term business success

You combine commercial understanding with technical curiosity

Success in this role requires more than pricing knowledge or system expertise alone. You enjoy working across disciplines and can comfortably move between commercial discussions, technical specifications, business processes, and stakeholder management. You are naturally curious, organised, and able to bring clarity to complex challenges.

We imagine that you have:

• 5+ years of experience within product ownership, business analysis, pricing, ERP, commercial systems, or related areas

• Experience translating business requirements into system capabilities and working closely with IT or development teams

• Understanding of pricing processes, commercial operations, revenue management, or Order-to-Cash processes

• Experience with ERP platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Oracle, or similar enterprise solutions

• Familiarity with agile methodologies, backlog management, sprint planning, or SAFe-based ways of working

• Strong analytical capabilities and an interest in data-driven decision-making and process optimisation

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills in a global environment

You know how to ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, and create practical solutions that balance business needs with technical possibilities. Equally important, you build strong relationships and work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of an international organisation.

Want to join the team?

Please submit your application no later than 25th of November. Please note we only accept applications submitted via our application system in accordance with the GDPR legislation.

• We aim to conduct 2nd round of interviews on Friday the 11th of December

Manager, Sales Training & Enablement – Hearing Aids

Location: Demant, Smørum

Turn commercial priorities into practical sales capabilities that make a measurable difference

Do you get energy from helping sales professionals build confidence, sharpen their skills and succeed with customers? Would you like to develop learning solutions that can be used across markets in a global organisation? Then this may be the opportunity for you.

As Manager, Sales Training & Enablement, you will translate commercial priorities and identified capability needs into relevant training programmes, learning journeys and practical tools.

You will manage initiatives from identifying needs and design through to delivery, implementation and follow-up, working closely with sales companies, business areas and colleagues across International Sales.

Welcome to Sales Training & Enablement

You will join a global Sales Training & Enablement team within International Sales. The team is a smaller international team with five colleagues having focus on sales training, sales product training and sales enablement. We work closely together in a collaborative, hands-on way, always keeping our target audience at the center of everything we do.

Turn learning into commercial impact

Our ambition is to make learning a competitive advantage by equipping the sales organisation with the skills, mindset and structure needed to create strong customer outcomes. Together with the team, you will ensure that training deliveries are practical, engaging, scalable and connected to the realities of sales performance.

We involve markets early, test ideas against business needs and focus on solutions that sales professionals and managers can apply in practice.

Your key responsibilities:

• Design, develop and deliver sales training programmes and learning journeys.

• Create and maintain digital learning activities and course content that support retention and application on the job on our FUSE platform.

• Conduct training-needs assessments with markets and stakeholders; analyse findings and recommend focused capability-building initiatives.

• Manage training projects end-to-end, including planning, content development, stakeholder coordination, implementation and follow-up.

• Facilitate engaging learning experiences in physical, virtual and blended formats for sales professionals

• Translate complex commercial concepts into simple, relevant and actionable content, tools and exercises.

• Coordinate with markets and business areas to adapt global solutions to relevant business needs while maintaining consistency and quality.

• Support the use and continuous improvement of learning technologies, authoring tools and learning-distribution platforms.

• Share best practices and contribute actively to global trainer and sales communities.

• Define appropriate success measures and use feedback and available performance indicators to improve learning solutions.

A commercially minded capability builder

You understand sales and enjoy helping others improve. You are comfortable owning projects independently, while involving the right stakeholders and creating alignment across functions and markets. You combine strong facilitation and communication skills with a structured approach to development and implementation.

What you will bring to the role:

• A relevant commercial or business background and approximately 3-5 years of experience within sales, sales training, sales enablement, facilitation and digital content creation.

Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

**About The Role

**We are looking for an Electrical & Instrumentation Engineer to join our Electrical & Instrumentation Department, consisting of approximately 100 engineers and specialists.

You will become part of a team of 100 engineers working across projects to design and deliver robust process control and instrumentation solutions for pharmaceutical facilities. Together, we cover everything from engineering design and specifications to testing, validation, and commissioning.

In this role, you will work closely with colleagues, vendors, and clients to ensure that electrical and instrumentation solutions meet both technical requirements and regulatory standards.

Please note that Danish language skills are required for this position.

Location Denmark - Kalundborg

Experience + 3 years

Department Electrical & Instrumentation

We’re looking for a Director of Revenue Operations (RevOps) to own the commercial operating system across the group's portfolio brands of Cookie Information, Piwik PRO and Sheltr. You will lead the commercial operating plan, the shared CRM and data, attribution, forecasting, and the objective arbitration of capacity across commercial teams. This role reports to the CCO.

The Director of RevOps is the key connective role between leadership and the commercial team leads, translating strategy into an operating plan they run with, and turning their execution data into insight leadership can act on to drive predictable, efficient and sustainable revenue growth.

We are open to on-site, hybrid, and remote working within two time zones of our offices (CET).

In this role, please expect to travel up to 40% of the time.

**About Us

**Our group brings together three European software brands that help organisations earn and use data with trust: Cookie Information for consent management; Piwik PRO for privacy-by-design analytics and data activation; and Sheltr for reliably finding personal data in internal data sources.

Headquartered in Copenhagen with an office in Wrocław, our team of 180 people have been building trusted data solutions since 2011. We work with companies and marketing teams across various industries that take control of their data model, including some of the most data-sensitive clients in healthcare, finance, energy & utilities, and the public sector. We are proud that our clients rely on us to meet GDPR and EU data residency requirements across EMEA and the US, as this regulatory depth is hard to build and replicate. We believe compliance and performance are not opposites. Consented data, auditable analytics and full visibility of personal data belong to one data journey; together they form a foundation that marketing, IT, legal and the C-level can rely on.

Our journey is to move from a regulation-driven house of brands to one unified company with a clear point of view. We are creating a new category around this complete data journey, and together we are building an enterprise-ready, data-driven revenue engine led by thought leadership. Want to join us on this journey? Keep reading to find out how you can help shape this with us.

The Role

As Director of RevOps, you will own the commercial revenue engine across all three brands, ensuring alignment between strategy, processes, technology and performance. You will build and lead a multidisciplinary team and act as a strategic partner to commercial leadership, driving operational excellence and turning insights into business outcomes.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Owning the commercial operating plan, revenue forecasting and pipeline performance across the portfolio, translating business objectives into clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

• Establish a shared CRM, account universe, campaign calendar and consistent funnel definitions, ensuring reliable data, clear processes and effective collaboration across brands.

• Driving data-led improvements in conversion, deal size, customer acquisition cost, customer lifetime value and return on investment. Lead reporting and performance reviews for the CCO, CEO and Finance.

• Providing an objective, data-driven perspective on commercial capacity and investment trade-offs, escalating key decisions to the CCO when needed.

• Owning the commercial technology stack, including HubSpot, BI, forecasting, marketing automation and AI, ensuring our tools and data enable scalable growth.

• Leading BI, marketing automation, customer and partner enablement, and product marketing. Partner with Product on feature prioritisation, pricing and packaging to strengthen go-to-market effectiveness.

**About You

**You are an experienced B2B SaaS RevOps leader who understands how to build a scalable, data-driven revenue engine. You combine strong commercial and financial acumen with analytical rigour and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Product and Finance.

You thrive in complex environments where you can bring structure, align competing priorities and turn data into better commercial decisions.

You bring:

• Significant experience leading Revenue Operations or owning the Sales and Marketing revenue engine in a B2B SaaS business.

• Strong commercial and financial understanding, including ARR, NRR, churn, CAC, customer lifetime value and payback.

• Deep expertise in pipeline management, funnel design, forecasting, attribution and performance optimisation.

• Advanced HubSpot expertise, including architecture, governance and process design.

• Experience with BI, marketing automation, AI and revenue technology.

• Experience leading multidisciplinary, hybrid-working teams and driving change across functions without relying solely on formal authority.

• Strong executive communication skills and the ability to influence C-level decision-making.

• Fluency in English (C2).

Nice-to-haves:

• Experience managing multi-brand or multi-product go-to-market operations on shared infrastructure.

• Experience with partner and channel models or account-based marketing.

• Familiarity with forecasting, conversation intelligence and advanced BI tools.

• Background in privacy, MarTech or analytics.

• Experience in a scale-up or PE- or VC-backed business.

• Fluency in German, French or a Nordic language.

What we offer

• Real ownership: Lead the commercial operating model across a three-brand portfolio.

• You’ll work closely with the CCO, CEO and commercial leadership to shape business priorities and decisions.

• You get to build shared systems, processes and insights that enable more effective and scalable commercial execution.

• A chance to make an impact: Strengthen how three growing SaaS brands plan, execute and scale their commercial growth through better data, processes and insights.

• Professional development budget, health insurance, and other benefits.

• A positive, informal workplace.

Application process

We’re looking to fill the position as soon as possible and will be inviting candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so don’t hesitate to send your application today.

This is what our recruitment process looks like:

• A brief screening call with our Talent Partner (online, approx. 30 mins)

• An in-depth interview with the hiring manager and a member of the team

• Interview with a key stakeholder including a live case

• A final interview with our CCO

This process is subject to change. All applicants who progress to the screening call will be informed of the full process as some stages may be combined and/or in person.

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

At Cookie Information & Piwik PRO we value diversity as a cornerstone of our success. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability. We recognise that certain groups are underrepresented in the tech industry, and we encourage everyone to apply and help us shape a more inclusive workspace.

Copenhagen, Denmark

_Want to put your financial markets expertise to work across exchanges, market data providers and multiple asset classes? Join Saxo’s Market Data & Exchange Relations team and take ownership in an area connecting markets, technology and commercial relationships.

_**About The Role

**This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of financial markets, market data, exchanges and technology in an international environment. You will collaborate with exchanges, market data providers and colleagues across Saxo, helping ensure that the data supporting our trading platforms and internal systems is managed effectively.

The Market Data & Exchange Relations team manages licensing and relationships with the external vendors and exchanges that provide market data to Saxo's trading platforms and internal systems.

Depending on your experience, you may bring established market data expertise to the team or relevant experience from another part of the financial sector and an interest in developing further within market data and exchange relations.

You will gain broad exposure to the financial markets value chain and work across multiple asset classes, including equities, futures, options and bonds.

The position involves collaboration across Saxo's international organisation, including commercial, operational, technology, finance and other specialist teams. You will also engage directly with exchanges and external data providers.

**Your Responsibilities

**Your responsibilities will include a combination of contract management, operational and commercial, including:

• Managing and maintaining relationships with market data vendors and exchanges, including licensing requirements and usage rights

• Negotiating, reviewing and maintaining market data licensing and vendor agreements, including commercial terms, permitted use and redistribution rights

• Acting as a point of contact for exchanges, vendors and other external partners

• Working with internal teams on billing, budgeting and reporting

• Monitoring and analysing market data usage, licensing permissions, entitlements and reporting obligations

• Supporting appropriate and compliant use of licensed market data across the organisation, in line with exchange and vendor licensing terms

• Providing market data licensing expertise and guidance to internal projects, new products and initiatives

• Managing day-to-day enquiries from internal and external stakeholders

• Supporting the ongoing development of processes and controls within the Market Data & Exchange Relations area

The scope and level of ownership can be adapted to your experience.

**Your profile

**We are interested in candidates with experience from market data, financial markets, exchanges, trading, financial services or a related field.

You may already be an experienced market data professional, or you may have developed relevant knowledge in another area of the financial sector and see market data as your next specialisation.

**We Expect That You

**

• Have relevant professional experience within financial services, market data or a related environment

• Have an interest in financial markets and how data supports trading and investment services

• Are comfortable working with contracts, data, processes and multiple stakeholders

• Take a structured and reliable approach to your work and can manage competing priorities

• Communicate effectively with both specialist and non-specialist stakeholders

• Are comfortable working with Excel, datasets and presentation tools and can learn new systems

• Can work independently while contributing to a collaborative team environment

• Are comfortable working in English in an international organisation

Experience working directly with market data vendors, stock exchanges, market data licensing, usage rights, redistribution, entitlements, reporting obligations or market data agreements would be valuable, but candidates with transferable experience from the wider financial sector are also encouraged to apply.

**An international role with broad market exposure

**This position provides an opportunity to develop a detailed understanding of how financial-market data moves from exchanges and providers into the systems and services used by investors and market participants.

You will work with colleagues and external partners across markets and functions, giving you exposure to both the commercial and operational aspects of market data.

Whether you bring several years of specialist experience or are looking to broaden your financial-markets expertise, the role offers the opportunity to take meaningful ownership while continuing to develop your knowledge.

The position is based at Saxo Bank's headquarters in Denmark.

**We get curious people invested in the world

We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

**Click here to create an account and upload your resume and a short motivation. We look forward to getting to know you better!

About DBI Plastics

DBI Plastics Group A/S is a family-owned Danish company with approximately 200 employees, developing and manufacturing protective solutions for the automotive, machinery and engineering industries. We manufacture in Stenmagle, Denmark, and Swidnica, Poland, and serve customers worldwide, supported by our own warehouses in Shanghai and Detroit. We are undergoing a strategic transformation with a clear ambition: to double the size of the business over the next five years. A significant share of this growth will come from a segment we have not historically approached systematically: the many small and medium-sized customers who currently buy on a transactional basis. This is why we are creating this role.

The role

As Head of Transactional Business, you will have full commercial responsibility for DBI’s global transactional business – revenue, margin and growth across all small and medium-sized customers. This is a business-building role: our channels are at different stages of maturity, and your task will be to structure, professionalise and scale them. You will work through two channels: our webshop and a dealer and distributor network that needs to expand. At the same time, you will transform customer service from a reactive function into a proactive, sales-driving team. As a member of the management team, you will contribute to DBI’s overall strategic direction – not just your own area.

Your responsibilities

• Commercial ownership. Full responsibility for sales, budgets and forecasts for the small and medium-sized customer segment. You set targets, track progress and deliver results.

• E-commerce. End-to-end ownership of the webshop – product range, pricing, conversion, customer journey and digital self-service experience. You run it as a business, not as an IT project.

• Marketplaces. We want to increase our visibility on marketplaces such as Amazon and Alibaba.

• EDI and digital integration. Expand EDI connections with small and medium-sized customers to create a seamless, scalable order flow in collaboration with our operations and IT teams.

• Distribution channels. Select, onboard, negotiate contracts with and manage the performance of distributors – supported by a clear channel strategy that avoids conflict with our direct business.

• Customer service-led outbound sales. Build a culture and operating model in which customer service actively drives sales through upselling, repeat-purchase cycles, reactivating dormant customers and qualifying leads.

• People leadership. Lead the team supporting our transactional channels, providing visible, clear leadership and well-defined decision-making responsibilities.

• Management team. Play an active role in DBI’s management team and share responsibility for delivering our ambition to double the size of the business.

Your profile

Essential experience

• Proven experience in driving e-commerce commercially – ideally in B2B – with responsibility for revenue and conversion, not just the platform.

• Experience in building and developing distribution channels: identifying, negotiating with and managing distributors or dealers.

• Experience in customer service-led outbound sales – you have personally helped transform a service team from reactive to proactive.

• Leadership experience with direct people management responsibility, ideally at management team level.

Skills and personal qualities

• This is a highly hands-on role with a small team, so you must enjoy working both strategically and at a very practical, operational level.

• You are data-driven and take a structured approach to KPIs, pipeline management and channel economics.

• You make decisions – even when information is incomplete – and communicate them in a way others can understand and act on.

• You are equally comfortable in an industrial manufacturing environment and working with a digital commercial agenda.

• You work across borders and cultures and understand how a global footprint shapes sales.

• You are fluent in spoken and written English.

What we offer

• A newly created role with a genuine mandate to shape an entire business area.

• A seat on the management team, with direct access to the Managing Director and a short path to decisions.

• A family-owned company with long-standing customer relationships, high quality standards and an ambitious growth plan.

• A competitive employment package reflecting the responsibilities of the role.

How to apply

Apply on www.dbiplastics.com by 16 November 2026. We review applications and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply early.
